the activity of serum lactate dehyrogenase in lambs infected by Dictyocaulis filaria is increased during the period of parasite patency and this increase is directly proportional to the intensity of lung lesions.
the LDH activity is increased in the serum of D filaria infected sheep and the level of increase in LDH activity is directly proportional to the severity of the disease.
serum LDH activity is of value as a biochemical marker in the assessment of the progress of the infection and the severity of lung damage caused by D filaria in lambs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LDH activity is a good indicator of the severity of lungworm infection.
serum lactate dehydrgenase is a good diagnostic and prognostic indicator of D filaria infection in sheep.
serum lactate dehyrogenase activity can be used as a reliable index of D filaria infection in lambs and that it may also prove to be of value in the diagnosis of D filaria infections in other hosts.

serum lactate dehyrogenase activity may be used as a non invasive method for earlier diagnosis, prognosis and monitoring of the disease in lambs.
